artifacts.summary: All five phases completed: one canonical required-heading contract established in report-format.md/summary-format.md, general-research-agent.md's verbatim copy converted to a pointer, all four formal research agents remediated (pointer + ## Recommendations promotion), fixture-verified red-to-green, and the cross-extension sweep's corrected enumeration recorded as follow-ups.

completion_data.completion_summary: Gave the four formal-extension research agents a reachable pointer at a new, single canonical required-heading contract in report-format.md/summary-format.md and promoted their buried ### Recommendations to a top-level ## Recommendations, closing the exact drift that let a real production report ship without the required heading. Converted general-research-agent.md's duplicate verbatim copy of the contract into a pointer at the same canonical section. Reproduced the production failure in a fixture (red before the remedy, green after), confirmed all four formal agents' skeletons pass the real validate-artifact.sh binary, and completed the cross-extension sweep scope item (4) scoped but never run, recording a corrected 15-agent domain-shaped gap count (vs. the research report's undercounted eleven/eight) plus the seven skeleton-less research agents as follow-ups.

memory_candidates.content: When reproducing a validate-artifact.sh heading check in a fixture or new prose, grep -c for the exact phrase as a verification step before trusting it: markdown line-wrapping can silently split a multi-word heading name (e.g. 'Recommended Next Steps') across two source lines, making a single-line grep match fail even though the words are present and readable. Caught this exact defect mid-task via the plan's own verification criterion.

When several agent files share one verbatim contract paragraph (e.g. required report-section headings), converting each copy into a pointer at one canonical section in a shared format-standard file (report-format.md/summary-format.md) prevents the copies from drifting independently -- the failure mode that let a core-extension agent get an updated contract while a sibling extension's agents kept the stale, buried version. Before deleting a verbatim copy, confirm the pointer target is actually reachable from that agent's own Context References load list, or the pointer becomes a dead link.
